verified: Settings → General → Software Update (iOS 26 and iOS 27 guides: "Tap General, then tap Software Update. The currently installed version of iOS is shown, and whether an update is available. If an update is available, tap Download and Install.")

spec: "If you see iOS 27 or iOS 26.7.1, either one is fine."
verified: Not a menu path. Version numbers are outside this verification pass; the release list at support.apple.com/100100 couldn't be parsed. The version-feed check has to confirm it.

spec: Settings → General → Software Update → Automatic Updates → turn on everything, including Security Responses & System Files
verified: Settings → General → Software Update → Automatic Updates. Under "iOS Updates", turn on "Automatically Install". ("Automatically Download" only appears after Automatically Install is turned off.) Under "System Files", turn on "Automatically Install". The iOS 26 and iOS 27 guides don't use the label "Security Responses & System Files" (that was the iOS 16–18 wording). Recommended copy: "Settings → General → Software Update → Automatic Updates → turn on Automatically Install (for iOS Updates and for System Files)."

spec: (not in spec) Security Responses assumed to live under Software Update
verified: Starting with iOS 26.1, between-release security fixes are called Background Security Improvements and live in a different place: Settings → Privacy & Security → Background Security Improvements → turn on "Automatically Install". Turning it off means "your device will not receive these improvements until they're included in a subsequent software update." Add this as a second step on the card, or as a separate check. (The iOS 26.0 guide's "Learn More" line says "Security Improvements", but the toggle step says "Background Security Improvements". Use the second.)

spec: Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Stolen Device Protection → On → Require Security Delay: Always
verified: Settings → Face ID & Passcode (on iPhone SE or a Home-button model: Touch ID & Passcode; the iOS 27 guide also lists iPhone Duo here) → enter passcode → scroll down → Stolen Device Protection → turn on → choose "Always" (the other option is "Away from Familiar Locations"). Support article wording: choose "Always" under Require Security Delay. If it isn't listed, set up Face ID or Touch ID first. It requires Find My, Significant Locations and two-factor authentication. Suggested addition: "You'll need to type your passcode on your iPhone." (This is the iPhone's own prompt, not Family Shield's. It fits the no-PIN footer, but the copy should make that clear.)

spec: "This may already be on. Just check." / "Changing some settings will take one hour. That's the point."
verified: Consistent with Apple: "Stolen Device Protection might be turned on by default" and a Security Delay is "a successful Face ID or Touch ID, an hour wait, then an additional successful biometric authentication."

spec: Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Account Recovery → Add Recovery Contact → Ben
verified: Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Recovery Contacts → Add Recovery Contact → follow the onscreen steps → pick Ben from the recommended contacts, or tap "Choose Someone Else". If Ben isn't in the Family Sharing group, he has to accept the invitation in Messages. Both people need iMessage turned on.

spec: AppleIDSettings link (Mac); path implied same as iOS
verified: Apple menu → System Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Recovery Contacts → Add Recovery Contact → follow the onscreen steps → Choose Someone Else if needed → Continue.

spec: "Choose a recovery contact, not a recovery key."
verified: Valid distinction. Apple documents both, and a recovery key is a separate 28-character code (Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security).

spec: Settings → Apps → Phone → Screen Unknown Callers → Ask Reason for Calling
verified: Settings → Apps → Phone → scroll to Screen Unknown Callers → Ask Reason for Calling (the options are Never, Ask Reason for Calling and Silence). This is identical in the iOS 26 and iOS 27 guides. Caveats: calls aren't screened while roaming, and screening turns off for 24 hours after you call emergency services.

spec: Settings → Apps → Messages → Screen Unknown Senders → On
verified: Settings → Apps → Messages → scroll down to Unknown Senders → turn on Screen Unknown Senders (iOS 26 support article). The iOS 27 guide only documents the in-app path: Messages → Filters button (top of the conversation list) → Manage Filtering → turn on Screen Unknown Senders. Adding that in-app path as the fallback covers both versions. Note that it's off by default in iOS 26 unless Filter Unknown Senders was on in iOS 18.

spec: Settings → [your name] → Find My → Find My iPhone → On (plus Find My network, Send Last Location)
verified: Settings → [your name] → Find My → Find My iPhone → turn on Find My iPhone. The same screen has Find My network and Send Last Location. This is identical in the iOS 26 and iOS 27 guides.

spec: Settings → Apps → Safari → Fraudulent Website Warning → On
verified: Settings → Apps → Safari → Fraudulent Website Warning → On. This is identical in iOS 26 and iOS 27. The iOS 27 guide adds "(Not available in all countries or regions.)"

spec: Settings → Privacy & Security → Safety Check → Manage Sharing & Access. "Don't use Emergency Reset unless you're in danger."
verified: Settings → Privacy & Security → Safety Check (you may need to scroll down) → Manage Sharing & Access → Continue → follow the onscreen instructions. Emergency Reset is the other option, and "Start Emergency Reset" is its button. Apple notes that Safety Check may work a little differently with Stolen Device Protection on.

spec: Passwords app → Security → fix or review any warnings
verified: Passwords app → Security → tap an account to see the warning → Change Password (or Hide, if it can't be fixed). In iOS 27, you may first have to tap the sidebar button to see the categories. Related setting: Settings → Apps → Passwords → Detect Compromised Passwords (on).

Settings → Face ID & Passcode (on iPhone SE or a Home-button model: Touch ID & Passcode; the iOS 27 guide also lists iPhone Duo) → Turn Passcode On. The copy has to show the Touch ID variant, because both apps detect the biometry type.
Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Set up Face ID (Touch ID models: Settings → Touch ID & Passcode). Choose the label from LAContext.biometryType.
